newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka parliament approves takeover six firms.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka parliament approves takeover six firms.

text.p: Sri Lanka's parliament on Wednesday approved the takeover by government of six firms said to have been mismanaged after privatisation.

Justice Minister and Deputy Finance Minister G.L. Peiris said the government was forced to take over the privatised firms under a new law because they had been mismanaged by the new owners and the workers were in dire straits.
The six firms were taken over under a law to rehabilitate public enterprises which was passed last October.
But Peiris assured foreign investors that there was no need for them to fear that the law would affect their investments as it had very limited scope.
Takeovers under the law were confined to state enterprises privatised by the previous government before the government set up its Public Enterprises Reform Commission (PERC), Peiris said.
He also said the government would not get involved in labour disputes in the six firms.
The six companies are Colombo Commercial Fertiliser, Hingurana Sugar Industries, Kahatagaha Graphite Lanka, Kantalai Sugar Industries, Lanka Loha Hardware and Mattegama Textiles Mills.
